findings.name: Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption
findings.description: Pennsylvania exempts the primary residence of an honorably discharged wartime veteran from real estate (property) tax if the veteran has a 100% permanent service-connected disability, total disability individual unemployability (TDIU), or service-connected blindness, paraplegia, or loss of two or more limbs, and demonstrates financial need. The exemption covers township, county, and school district real estate taxes on the veteran's principal dwelling, owned solely by the veteran or jointly with a spouse.
findings.value: Full exemption from real estate tax on the veteran's primary residence, subject to a financial-need determination by the State Veterans' Commission
otherReqs: Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge
Service during a period of war as determined by the U.S. VA
Real estate occupied as the veteran's principal dwelling
Alternate qualifying conditions: service-connected blindness, paraplegia, or loss of two or more limbs (in place of 100% P&T rating)
Financial need: household income at or below $114,637 (as of Jan. 1, 2025) creates a presumption of need; higher-income applicants may still qualify if allowable expenses exceed income
Unmarried surviving spouse may continue or newly qualify for the exemption
findings.agency: PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA) / Pennsylvania State Veterans' Commission
documentation: VA disability rating decision letter
DD-214 or other discharge documentation
Proof of Pennsylvania residency
Financial/income documentation for the need determination
findings.legalCitation: 51 Pa.C.S. (Title 51, Military Affairs); 43 Pa. Code Subchapter C (Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption Program)
findings.sourceExcerpt: 100 percent permanent service-connected disability, total disability individual unemployability, or service-connected blindness, paraplegia, or loss of two or more limbs ... $114,637 or less are given a presumption of need for the exemption.

findings.name: Pennsylvania Veterans Homes
findings.description: The PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs operates six state veterans' homes offering long-term nursing, personal, domiciliary, and memory care for eligible veterans and, at some facilities, their spouses. Facilities are located in Philadelphia, Lackawanna, Blair, Erie, Chester, and Allegheny counties, with not all levels of care available at every location.
findings.value: Long-term residential and nursing care at six state-operated veterans' homes
otherReqs: Meets medical, financial, and military-service admission criteria set by the individual home
Veteran or, at some facilities, veteran's spouse
findings.agency: PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service
findings.sourceExcerpt: If you served our country, love to show your patriotism and need long-term care, then one of Pennsylvania's six Veterans Homes is the ideal place for you and/or your spouse to call home.

findings.name: Educational Gratuity Program
findings.description: Pennsylvania pays a tuition gratuity toward the education of children of veterans who are 100% permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition (wartime service), or whose veteran-parent died or was killed in service during a period of war or armed conflict. The child must be age 16-23, have lived in Pennsylvania for the five years before applying, attend an approved school within the Commonwealth, and demonstrate financial need.
findings.value: Up to $500 per term or semester per qualified child, paid directly to the approved educational institution, for a maximum of four scholastic years (eight payments)
otherReqs: Child must be between ages 16 and 23
Child must have lived in Pennsylvania for the five years prior to application
Child must attend an approved school within the Commonwealth
Financial need required
Veteran-parent must be 100% P&T service-connected disabled, OR have died / been killed in service during a period of war or armed conflict
findings.agency: PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
documentation: DD-214 or Military Death Certificate
Child's birth certificate
Photo identification
Proof of Pennsylvania residency for the last five years
findings.sourceExcerpt: Payment will not exceed $500 per term or semester per qualified child to each approved educational institution ... may not be made for longer than four scholastic years (eight payments).

findings.name: Veterans' Preference in Civil Service Employment
findings.description: Pennsylvania law adds 10 points to a qualifying veteran's civil service examination score for Commonwealth positions, and requires appointing authorities to give hiring preference to veterans on certified eligible lists. The preference does not apply to promotions or internal civil service postings. A related preference extends to the surviving spouse of a deceased service member, or the spouse of a veteran the VA has classified as permanently and totally disabled.
findings.value: 10 additional points added to the civil service examination score, plus preference in appointment from certified eligible lists
otherReqs: Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge (or currently serving in specified circumstances)
Does not apply to promotions or internal civil service postings
Spousal preference available for surviving spouses, or spouses of veterans rated permanent and total by the VA
findings.agency: PA State Civil Service Commission / Governor's Office of Administration
documentation: VA disability rating decision letter (for spousal preference based on permanent total disability)
findings.sourceExcerpt: An additional 10 points shall be added to the veteran's final examination score ... the appointing authority in making an appointment to a public position shall give preference to the veteran.

findings.name: Free Vehicle Registration for Eligible Veterans
findings.description: Pennsylvania waives the registration and title fees (license plate fees still apply) for one passenger vehicle or truck weighing 9,000 pounds or less owned by a veteran who lost a limb or eye or became partially paralyzed while serving in the U.S. Armed Forces. The same fee waiver applies to former prisoners of war, Congressional Medal of Honor recipients, and Purple Heart recipients.
findings.value: Registration and title fee waiver for one qualifying vehicle; license plate fees still apply
otherReqs: Lost a limb or eye, or became partially paralyzed, while serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, OR
Former prisoner of war in a conflict for which DoD authorizes a campaign medal, OR
Congressional Medal of Honor recipient, OR
Purple Heart recipient
Applies to one qualifying vehicle only
findings.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT), Bureau of Motor Vehicles
documentation: Proof of qualifying condition or award (VA certification, DoD/military documentation)
findings.sourceExcerpt: A veteran who lost a limb or eye or who became partially paralyzed while serving in the Armed Forces of the United States ... A person who has been awarded the Congressional Medal of Honor ... A person who has been awarded the Purple Heart. License plate fees still apply.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran / Severely Disabled Veteran Registration Plate
findings.description: PennDOT issues a special Disabled Veteran registration plate to a veteran with a disability certified by their service unit or the VA, and a Severely Disabled Veteran plate to a veteran with a 100% service-connected disability. Both plates allow the vehicle to park up to 60 minutes beyond the posted legal parking period in addition to standard accessible-parking privileges.
findings.value: Special disabled-veteran license plate; extends legal parking time by 60 minutes beyond posted limits
otherReqs: Disabled Veteran plate: disability certified by service unit or VA (no stated percentage minimum)
Severely Disabled Veteran plate: 100% service-connected disability certified by the VA
findings.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT), Bureau of Motor Vehicles
documentation: VA or military service-unit disability certification
findings.sourceExcerpt: If a veteran applying has a disability certified by their service unit or the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, PennDOT will issue a special registration plate ... PennDOT will issue a special plate for a veteran with a 100% service-connected disability.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting and Furtaker License
findings.description: Pennsylvania provides a fee exemption on a Regular Hunting and Furtaker License for a resident veteran of any war or armed conflict who has a service-connected loss of one or more limbs, loss of use of one or more limbs, or is medically certified as totally disabled, provided the veteran is otherwise mentally and physically fit to hunt. The official Game Commission page confirms a license fee exemption exists but does not state a specific dollar fee or disability rating percentage, so those figures are omitted rather than guessed.
findings.value: License fee exemption for qualifying disabled veterans; exact dollar fee not stated on the official page
otherReqs: Veteran of any war or armed conflict
Service-connected loss of one or more limbs, loss of use of one or more limbs, or medically certified as totally disabled
Must be otherwise mentally and physically fit
Must meet all other requirements of the Game and Wildlife Code
documentation: Discharge papers
VA disability certification (for total-disability claim)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Loss of one or more limbs, or the loss of the use of one or more limbs, or medically certified as totally disabled ... Disability was service incurred ... Must be a veteran of any war or armed conflict.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Fishing License
findings.description: Pennsylvania resident veterans with a service-connected disability rated 100% by the VA receive a free annual fishing license (plus a free Combination Trout/Lake Erie Permit); veterans rated 60-99% service-connected disabled qualify for a reduced-fee resident annual or senior resident lifetime fishing license. Exact reduced-fee dollar amount is not stated on the official page and is omitted rather than guessed.
findings.value: Free fishing license (100% rated) or reduced-fee license (60-99% rated); free Combination Trout/Lake Erie Permit for 100%-rated veterans
otherReqs: Bona fide Pennsylvania resident
Service-connected disability certified by the VA
100% disabled: free license; 60-99% disabled: reduced-fee license
documentation: Written certification from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
Proof of Pennsylvania residency (e.g., driver's license)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Be a bona fide resident of Pennsylvania ... 100% disabled as certified by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) ... 60 to 99% disabled as certified by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

findings.name: Blind Veterans Pension and Amputee & Paralyzed Veterans Pension
findings.description: Pennsylvania pays a monthly pension of $150 to eligible veterans who were Pennsylvania residents upon entering the military, received an honorable discharge, and have a qualifying service-connected condition: for the Blind Veterans Pension, visual acuity of 3/60 (10/200) or worse in the better eye (or comparably restricted visual field); for the Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension, loss or loss of use of two or more extremities with a VA rating of at least 40% in each affected limb.
otherReqs: Resident of Pennsylvania upon entering the military
Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge
Blind Veterans Pension: visual acuity 3/60 (10/200) or worse in the better eye, or visual field contracted to 20 degrees or less
Amputee/Paralyzed Veterans Pension: service-connected loss or loss of use of two or more extremities, each rated at least 40% by the VA
findings.agency: PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
documentation: Proof of Pennsylvania residency at time of military entry
VA decision letter documenting the qualifying disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: This program provides eligible veterans with a monthly pension of $150 ... visual acuity with correcting lens is 3/60 or 10/200 or equivalent, or less normal vision in the better eye.
